headline: Two healthcare data thefts surfaced in a day, exposing more than 24 million dental and medical patients as DentaQuest and MCBS disclosed intrusions.

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews and quiet data thieves keep mining medical records, with DentaQuest exposing over 23 million people and the PEAR group claiming 3 terabytes from MCBS.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Dental and Medical Breaches Expose 24 Million

emerging_trends.text: Package registries now slow themselves down on purpose, as GitHub's three-day Dependabot cooldown buys defenders time to catch poisoned releases before automation adopts them.
Defenders race to fence in AI coding agents that inherit their operator's every credential, pushing open-source sandboxes like Nono into the toolchain.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Nono Sandboxes AI Agents' Credential Reach

topics.title: GitHub Sets Three-Day Dependabot Cooldown
topics.latest_developments: GitHub detailed on July 27, 2026 that its new Dependabot cooldown waits at least three days after a release publishes before opening a pull request, and cited the September 2025 npm attack that phished a maintainer and poisoned chalk, debug, and roughly a dozen packages downloaded over 2 billion times a week.
topics.summary: GitHub's configurable three-day Dependabot cooldown delays automatic adoption of fresh package versions so defenders can catch poisoned releases first. Teams can tune the window in dependabot.yml to fit their tolerance for update lag.

sources.title: GitHub Adds 3-Day Dependabot Cooldown to Limit Poisoned Package Adoption
GitHub delays version updates so malware gets caught first
GitHub, PyPI add time-based defenses against supply chain attacks

topics.title: Dental and Medical Breaches Expose 24 Million
topics.latest_developments: DentaQuest disclosed on July 27, 2026 that a May 2026 intrusion stole personal and dental-health data on more than 23 million people, and SecurityWeek reported the PEAR ransomware group claimed 3 terabytes from medical business management firm MCBS, hitting 1.2 million individuals.
topics.summary: DentaQuest, a dental-benefits administrator, lost personal and dental-health records on over 23 million people; MCBS, a medical business management company, saw PEAR claim 3 terabytes covering 1.2 million people. Affected patients should watch for medical-identity fraud and enroll in any monitoring offered.

sources.title: DentaQuest Data Breach Potentially Impacts Over 23 Million People
MCBS Data Breach Affects 1.2 Million Individuals

topics.title: TELESHIM Malware Abuses Telegram Against Mideast Governments
topics.latest_developments: Zscaler ThreatLabz reported on July 27, 2026 that a threat actor with East Asia ties targeted Middle East government entities earlier this month, dropping three previously unreported malware families—TELESHIM, MIXEDKEY, and BINDCLOAK—with TELESHIM routing command-and-control through Telegram.
topics.summary: A suspected East Asian actor breached Middle East government networks and deployed the new TELESHIM, MIXEDKEY, and BINDCLOAK implants, using Telegram as a covert C2 channel. Government defenders in the region should hunt for Telegram-based traffic and these signatures.

sources.title: TELESHIM Abuses Telegram for C2 in Attacks Against Middle East Governments

topics.title: Nono Sandboxes AI Agents' Credential Reach
topics.latest_developments: Help Net Security profiled Nono on July 27, 2026, a free open-source sandbox that isolates AI coding agents which otherwise run with their launcher's full permissions and can read every file and live cloud key in the environment.
topics.summary: AI coding agents inherit the operator's access, so a prompt injection, mistyped command, or hallucinated path can point that reach at a company's own credentials. Nono confines the agent to blunt that damage; teams running agentic tools can adopt it now.

sources.title: Nono: Open-source sandbox for AI agents

topics.title: Scanners Hunt ESAFENET CDG Weak Logins
topics.latest_developments: The SANS Internet Storm Center reported on July 26, 2026 renewed scanning for weak logins on ESAFENET's CDG 3 Content Data Guard, a document-management and data-leak-prevention product aimed at the Chinese market that carries SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and default passwords.
topics.summary: ESAFENET CDG 3, a Chinese-market secure document-management product, ships with default passwords and injection flaws, and attackers are probing internet-exposed instances for weak credentials. Operators should change defaults and pull the consoles off the public internet.

sources.title: Scans for ESAFENET CDG 3 Document Management System Weak Logins

business_politics.title: Oil Plunges as U.S. and Iran Pause Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude fell about 8% back below $90 a barrel as the two sides held their strike pause for a second day and signaled diplomacy, with U.S. stock futures rallying and Treasury yields and the dollar sliding.
business_politics.summary: The United States and Iran refrained from military strikes across the Persian Gulf for a second straight day, easing fears over the Strait of Hormuz and reviving hopes of ending the five-month conflict; crude retreated from above $100 a barrel, lifting global equities and gold while pressuring the dollar.
